name: Medial FCU-split approach to the coronoid
aliases: flexor carpi ulnaris split approach to the coronoid
corridor: Medial approach unroofing the ulnar nerve and splitting the two heads of flexor carpi ulnaris to reach the anteromedial coronoid facet, sublime tubercle, and medial collateral ligament

positioning.text: Position supine with the arm on a hand table and the shoulder externally rotated, or across the chest, so the medial elbow is accessible.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the medial epicondyle, the sublime tubercle, and the course of the ulnar nerve between the two heads of flexor carpi ulnaris.

incision.text: Use a posterior incision with a medial flap or a direct medial incision, protecting the posterior branches of the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve.

superficial_interval.text: Identify the ulnar nerve and unroof it about 6 cm proximal and distal to the epicondyle, starting proximally where it is safer, and transpose it anteriorly and subcutaneously if that is safer.

deep_interval.text: Split the two heads of flexor carpi ulnaris along the ulnar nerve and elevate the humeral head extraperiosteally off the coronoid, medial collateral ligament, and anterior capsule, starting distally.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve, the ulnar nerve, the two heads of flexor carpi ulnaris, and the anteromedial coronoid.

structures_at_risk.text: The ulnar nerve between the FCU heads, the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve, and the medial collateral ligament are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The cubital tunnel and the interval between the FCU heads are the danger zone for the ulnar nerve and its first motor branch.

retraction_hazards.text: Protect the unroofed ulnar nerve throughout and preserve the medial collateral ligament by staying extraperiosteal.

exposure.text: Exposes the anteromedial facet of the coronoid, the sublime tubercle, and the medial collateral ligament.

limitations.text: Exposure is medial; further reach requires additional FCU splitting or flexor-pronator elevation.

indications.text: Indicated for fixation of anteromedial facet coronoid fractures.

closure.text: Repair the FCU heads, ensure the transposed or in-situ ulnar nerve lies in a healthy bed, and close in layers.

complications.text: Complications include ulnar neuropathy, medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve injury, and medial collateral ligament insufficiency.

procedure_applications.condition: An anteromedial facet coronoid fracture needs medial exposure

questions.question: What does the FCU-split approach expose best?
questions.answer: The anteromedial facet of the coronoid, the sublime tubercle, and the medial collateral ligament.

questions.question: How far is the ulnar nerve unroofed?
questions.answer: About 6 cm proximal and distal to the medial epicondyle.

questions.question: Where is ulnar nerve exposure begun and why?
questions.answer: Proximally, because it is easier and safer to identify the nerve there.
